```{r, load libraries}
#| output: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(psych)
library(gt)
library(janitor)
```

```{r, load data}
#| output: FALSE

#load data
data <- read_excel("./Attachment_Anxiety_Data.xlsx")
#inspect data
head(data)
```

```{r, clean data}
#| output: FALSE

attach_anx.clean <- data |> 
mutate(Gender = case_when(Gender == 1 ~ "Male", Gender == 2 ~ "Female")) |> 
mutate(`Age group` = case_when(`Age group` == 1 ~ "18-24", `Age group` == 2 ~ "24-34", `Age group` == 3 ~ "35-44", `Age group` == 4 ~ "45-54", `Age group` == 5 ~ "55-64" )) |> 
mutate(Relationship = case_when(Relationship == 1 ~ "married", Relationship == 2 ~ "in a relationship", Relationship == 4 ~ "divorced", Relationship == 5 ~ "not in a relationship", Relationship == 6 ~ "never been in a relationship", Relationship == 7 ~ "prefer not to say")) |> 
mutate(Ethnicity = case_when(Ethnicity == 1 ~ "white/Caucasian", Ethnicity == 2 ~ "Asian/Asian British", Ethnicity == 5 ~ "Other ethnic group", Ethnicity == 6 ~ "prefer not to say")) |> 
select(Gender, `Age group`, Relationship, Ethnicity, SA_1:SEst_10) |> 
mutate_at(5:43, as.integer)
```

```{r, score items}
#| output: FALSE

# define scales
social_interaction_keys <- list(social_interaction = c("SA_1","SA_2","SA_3","SA_4","-SA_5","SA_6","SA_7","SA_8","-SA_9","SA_10","-SA_11","SA_12","SA_13","SA_14","SA_15","SA_16","SA_17","SA_18","SA_19","SA_20"))
close_relationship_keys <- list(close_relationships = c("AA_1","AA_2","AA_3","AA_4","AA_5","AA_6","AA_7","AA_8","AA_9"))
self_esteem_keys <- list(self_esteem = c("SEst_1","-SEst_2","SEst_3","SEst_4","-SEst_5","-SEst_6","SEst_7","-SEst_8","-SEst_9","SEst_10"))

#compute Cronbach's alpha and average scores
social_interaction_scores <- scoreItems(social_interaction_keys, attach_anx.clean, totals = F, min=0, max=4)
close_relationship_scores <- scoreItems(close_relationship_keys, attach_anx.clean, totals = F, min=1, max=7)
self_esteem_scores <- scoreItems(self_esteem_keys, attach_anx.clean, totals=F, min=1, max=4)

#convert new scores into individual dataframes
social_interaction_scores.df <- as.data.frame(social_interaction_scores$scores)
close_relationship_scores.df <- as.data.frame(close_relationship_scores$scores)
self_esteem_scores.df <- as.data.frame(self_esteem_scores$scores)
```

```{r, combine dataframes}
#| output: FALSE

#combine into one dataframe
allscores.df <- cbind(social_interaction_scores.df, close_relationship_scores.df, self_esteem_scores.df)
combineall.df <- cbind(allscores.df, attach_anx.clean)
```

```{r, reduce data}
#| output: FALSE

# select only variables of interest
attach_anx.final <- combineall.df |> 
select("Gender", `Age group`, "Relationship", "Ethnicity", "social_interaction", "close_relationships", "self_esteem")
```

```{r, reproducible table of relationship by age group}
#| output: FALSE

# Create a demographics table of relationship status by age group
demographic_table <- attach_anx.final |> 
tabyl(`Age group`, Relationship)

# Create reproducible gt table
gttable.1 <- demographic_table |>
gt() |> 
tab_header(
    title = md("Distribution of Relationship Status by Age Group")) |> 
cols_width(
    everything() ~ pct(14.3)) |> 
tab_spanner(
    label="Relationship Status",
    columns = c(divorced:`prefer not to say`)
)

```

```{r, reproducible table for 3 Attachment and Social Anxiety Scales}
#| output: FALSE

#round alpha values to 2 decimals
alphas <- round(c(social_interaction_scores$alpha,
close_relationship_scores$alpha,
self_esteem_scores$alpha), 2)

#summary statistics for the three scales
summary <- describe(select(attach_anx.final, social_interaction:self_esteem))
summary

#sample size label
n <- (describe(attach_anx.final))[1,2]

#create a column for the scales in the summary table
Scales <- c("social_interaction", "close_relationships", "self_esteem")
summary$Scales <- Scales

#keep only selected columns
summary <- summary |> 
select(Scales, mean, median, sd, range) |> 
mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

#combine summary with alphas
summary.table <- cbind(summary, alphas)

# Create reproducable summary table with alphas
gttable.2 <- gt(summary.table) |> 
tab_header(
    title = md("*Descriptive Statistics for Three Attachment and Social Anixety Instruments*")) |> 
tab_stubhead(label= "Composites") |> 
tab_spanner(
        label= "Central Tendency",
        columns = c(mean, median)
) |> 
        tab_spanner(
label= "Variability",
columns = c(sd, range)
        ) |> 
tab_spanner(
            label = "Reliability Values (Cronbach's alpha)",
            columns = c(alphas)
)
```

```{r, filter dataset}
#| output: FALSE

# Filter dataset to one demographic variable -  extract only participants in a relationship
attach_anx.filtered <- attach_anx.final |> 
filter(Relationship == "in a relationship")

table(attach_anx.filtered$Relationship)
```

```{r, reproducible table for filtered scale scores}
#| output: FALSE

#round filtered alphas to 2 decimals
alphas_filtered <- round(c(
social_interaction_scores$alpha,
close_relationship_scores$alpha,
self_esteem_scores$alpha), 2)

#summary statistics
summary_filtered <- describe(select(attach_anx.filtered, social_interaction:self_esteem))
summary_filtered

#create column for scales
Scales <- c("social_interaction", "close_relationships", "self_esteem")
summary_filtered$Scales <- Scales

#select columns of interest
summary_filtered <- summary_filtered |> 
select(Scales, mean, median, sd, range) |> 
mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

#combine filtered summary and filtered alphas
filtered_summary_table <- cbind(summary_filtered, alphas_filtered)

#create the reproducible gt table
gttable.3 <- gt(filtered_summary_table) |> 
tab_header(
    title = md("*Descriptive Statistics for Attachment and Social Anxiety Inventories for People in Relationships*")) |> 
tab_stubhead(label= "Composites")|>
    tab_spanner(
        label="Central Tendency",
        columns = c(mean, median)
    )|>
        tab_spanner(
        label="Variability",
        columns = c(sd, range)
        )|>
            tab_spanner(
        label="Reliability Values (Chronbach's alpha)",
        columns = c(alphas_filtered)
            ) 
```

## Introduction


## Methods

### Participants

This dataset contains responses from `{r} n <- (describe(attach_anx.final))[1,2]` participants across a variety of relationship statuses and age groups (Table 1).

`{r} gttable.1`


### Measures

This dataset contains responses from three Inventories related to attachment and social anxiety. The Social Interaction Anxiety Scale is a 20-item inventory that measures the degree to which individuals experience anxiety in social environments (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[1]`). The Experiences in Close Relationships Scale is a shortened, 9-item inventory which measures attachment-related anxiety (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[2]`). Finally, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale is a 10-item scale that contains questions on one's self-esteem (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[3]`).

### Data Analysis Strategy

Both the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale contain items that were reverse-scored. Specifically, the data for variables SA_5, SA_9, SA_11, SEst_2, SEst_5, SEst_6, SEst_8, and SEst_9 were reverse keyed.

## Results

`{r} gttable.2`

Overall descriptive statistics were calculated for the three scales in the dataset. Participants had a mean score of `{r} summary.table[1,2]` on the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, `{r} summary.table[2,2]` on the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale, and `{r} summary.table[3,2]` on the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale.

`{r} gttable.3`

When only including participants in a relationship, participants had a mean score of `{r} filtered_summary_table[1,2]` on the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, a mean score of `{r} filtered_summary_table[2,2]` on the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale, and a mean score of `{r} filtered_summary_table[3,2]` on the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale.
